variants.name: Scoped enumeration (enum class)
variants.idiom_name: enum class with fixed underlying type
variants.implementation_notes: enum class eliminates the two holes that made C++03 enums unsafe: there is no implicit conversion to or from integral types, and the enumerators live in the enum's own scope, so two sets cannot be mixed. Give the enum an explicit underlying type whenever the value crosses a serialization or ABI boundary, and keep conversion to integers behind a validating boundary function (static_cast does not check). This is the default realization; the C++03 class-wrapper idiom remains only for pre-C++11 toolchains.
pitfalls: static_cast<Suit>(raw) from an unchecked integer compiles for every value - validate first, convert once, at the boundary.
A `using enum Suit;` (C++20) declaration re-injects the enumerator names into the enclosing scope and brings back the scoping problem.
Changing the underlying type changes the ABI and the meaning of serialized values; pin it deliberately.

variants.name: Class wrapper with static const instances (pre-C++11)
variants.idiom_name: More C++ Idioms 'Type Safe Enum' (safe_enum wrapper)
variants.implementation_notes: For C++03 toolchains: wrap a private enum in a class that exposes one static const instance per value and no implicit conversion operator, so only declared members can be passed and comparison operators are explicit. The template form (safe_enum<def, inner>) additionally lets you choose the underlying representation portably. Use it only where enum class is unavailable; it costs boilerplate and still permits casting if you expose the inner type.
pitfalls: Exposing the inner enum or a conversion operator reopens the implicit-conversion hole the wrapper exists to close.
Static const instances in headers risk multiple-definition/ODR problems; define them in one translation unit.
No exhaustiveness checking exists over the wrapper; switches must go through an explicit toInt()/underlying() accessor and a matching enum.
